objections.claim: The canonical freshness digest covers only `(path ‖ blob-digest)` pairs, but the woven artifact also depends on Git history: the git weaver emits history-derived facts such as `introduced-by` commit identities. A checkout with identical woven file blobs but rewritten/cherry-picked history therefore has the same input_closure_digest and source refs, so default `--verify-committed` can accept a snapshot whose history-derived edges differ from a fresh weave; the producer-bound check only proves where that insufficient verifier ran. Include every history-sensitive semantic input in a digest stable across the generated-evidence commit (for example, a canonical path-limited history closure), or re-derive and compare all history-derived outputs, and add an identical-tree/different-history regression. Candidate plan_ref sha256:659a062bf7ba80d822f9ed39b77dd0c1c42b670bfb41bd6a17a9e7f46cbcf2cb.

The all-tracked-text scanner and its two dispositions cannot honestly reach the promised clean sweep. Current tracked dependency metadata such as `narcissus/flagship/package-lock.json` contains many real Node compatibility claims below 22.12 (for example dependency `engines.node` values of `>=18`); these are neither false positives nor historical immutable product artifacts, and rewriting third-party engine metadata would be incorrect. Add a closed, machine-preconditioned classification for third-party compatibility metadata, or semantically exclude parsed dependency metadata while still rejecting project/operator runtime-floor claims, with fixtures proving a top-level product claim cannot use that classification. Candidate plan_ref sha256:659a062bf7ba80d822f9ed39b77dd0c1c42b670bfb41bd6a17a9e7f46cbcf2cb.
